## REQ-001 — Axolotl Character Controller — Dual Movement Grammars <!-- r:REQ-001 -->
status: in-progress · criteria 6/7 · tasks 0/12 · tests 6/0/0 of 6
### Criteria
- [x] Crossing a water volume boundary switches movement grammar in the same physics frame as the crossing, with no frame rendered in the previous grammar, and retains momentum magnitude per tuning key controller.transition.momentum_retention_ratio
  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-001-1 ✅
- [x] Water grammar supports full 3D directional swimming, dive, and a bubble boost governed by a cooldown
  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-001-2 ✅
- [x] Land grammar supports waddle locomotion, hop, and climbing on surfaces tagged as climbable
  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-001-3 ✅
- [x] Tongue grapple attaches to anchor points at or within tuning key controller.grapple.max_range_m, rejects anchors beyond it, and pulls the axolotl to the attached anchor
  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-001-4 ✅
- [x] Water-powered dash is usable in both grammars, consumes a charge, and recharges only while in water
  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-001-5 ✅
- [x] Controller exposes a documented public interface (movement state, capability modifiers, ability hooks) that worlds bind to without modifying controller internals
  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-001-6 ✅
- [ ] Both movement grammars feel distinct, responsive, and pleasurable in hands-on play
  ↳ tasks: T10 ☐ (Axolotl Controller)

## REQ-002 — Regeneration and Capability Loss System <!-- r:REQ-002 -->
status: in-progress · criteria 6/7 · tasks 0/14 · tests 6/0/0 of 6
### Criteria
- [x] Damage from enemies and non-catastrophic hazards strips a specific capability rather than reducing a health value
  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-002-1 ✅
- [x] Each capability loss applies a defined, measurable movement modifier: tail reduces swim speed, gill reduces boost duration, leg reduces climb height
  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-002-2 ✅
- [x] Capability loss alone never triggers a life loss, a death, or a run reset under any combination of losses
  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-002-3 ✅
- [x] Regen stations restore all lost capabilities on use
  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-002-4 ✅
- [x] Regen stations can apply a temporary mutation loadout that alters the axolotl configuration for the duration given by tuning key regen.mutation.duration_s, after which the axolotl reverts to its base configuration
  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-002-5 ✅
- [x] Capability state is fully restored when the player respawns at a checkpoint
  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-002-6 ✅
- [ ] Each loss and regrowth plays comedic, non-gruesome feedback consistent with the family-appropriate tone
  ↳ tasks: T10 ☐ (Regeneration and Capability System)

## REQ-003 — Lives, Checkpoints and Hard Failure State <!-- r:REQ-003 -->
status: in-progress · criteria 7/8 · tasks 0/11 · tests 7/0/0 of 7
### Criteria
- [x] Lives decrement only from designated catastrophic sources: pit volumes, crush hazards, boss finishers, and Dredger area-wipe attacks
  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-003-1 ✅
- [x] Ordinary enemy and hazard contact never decrements lives
  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-003-2 ✅
- [x] Reaching zero lives respawns the player at the last activated checkpoint with the life count replenished
  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-003-3 ✅
- [x] Reaching zero lives never restarts the world from the beginning and never modifies or penalizes the save file
  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-003-4 ✅
- [x] Activating a checkpoint records respawn position and restores both life count and capability state
  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-003-5 ✅
- [x] A world can declare a lives-per-attempt override through the Level Contract, and the global default applies when it does not
  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-003-6 ✅
- [x] Checkpoint spacing in every official world keeps the replay time from any checkpoint to the next at or below tuning key progression.max_retry_seconds
  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-003-7 ✅
- [ ] Losing all lives reads as a meaningful setback without feeling punishing, across repeated play
  ↳ tasks: T10 ☐ (Lives and Checkpoint System)

status: in-progress · criteria 6/10 · tasks 0/36 · tests 6/0/0 of 6

  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-006-3 ✅

  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-006-4 ✅

  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-006-5 ✅
- [x] Schema enumerates the sanctioned world API surface that a world module may call
  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-006-6 ✅
- [ ] A prose contract document explains every schema element and its rationale for human contributors
  ↳ tasks: T16 ☐ (OpenAxolotl Game Client)
- [ ] A documented migration path describes how a v1 world is brought forward when the contract version increments
  ↳ tasks: T17 ☐ (OpenAxolotl Game Client)
- [ ] A contributor unfamiliar with the codebase can produce a conforming world from the contract document alone
  ↳ tasks: T18 ☐ (OpenAxolotl Game Client)

## REQ-037 — Platformer jump feel and climb robustness <!-- r:REQ-037 -->
status: verified (smoke) · criteria 7/7 · tasks 0/28 · tests 7/0/0 of 7
### Criteria
- [x] Coyote time forgives a hop pressed just after leaving a ledge, expires after the tuned window, and is spent by firing so a hop can never chain into a mid-air ascent
  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-037-1 ✅
- [x] A hop pressed in mid-air is buffered on the rising edge only and fires on touchdown; the buffer expires rather than firing late, and holding the button does not refill it
  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-037-2 ✅
- [x] Releasing the hop mid-rise cuts the vertical speed by the tuned ratio; the cut never touches a descent, a rise the hop did not start, or a rise whose button is still held — proven through the real controller, where a tapped jump measurably rises less than a held one
  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-037-3 ✅
- [x] PlayerIntent carries a sustained verb set alongside the edge-triggered one: a held key sustains its verb until release, re-resolves under the live grammar (SPACE held through the water/land seam sustains what it means now), and is dropped on a device switch and on clear()
  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-037-4 ✅
- [x] A climber presses into the wall at the tuned adhesion on every frame — steering up, sideways, and clinging still — so motion along the surface cannot end the climb by starving it of contact, and the greybox smoke proves the climb rises in a real scene
  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-037-5 ✅
- [x] Losing wall contact for less than the tuned grace does not end a climb and regaining the wall resets the window; contact lost past the grace releases exactly once
  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-037-6 ✅
- [x] Every window, ratio and speed above is a tuning key with documented unit and range, and the greybox smoke and coral walk complete against the retuned arc
  ↳ tests: TC-REQ-037-7 ✅

## REQ-041 — Hero anatomy fidelity: the maintainer's reference sheet, built <!-- r:REQ-041 -->
status: in-progress · criteria 2/6 · tasks 0/0 · tests 6/0/0 of 6
### Criteria
- [ ] The gill plumes have volume rather than lying in a plane: measured over one side's plume in the shipped model, the smallest principal spread of the filament mass is at least 0.22 of the largest. THE BAR MOVED WITH THE DESIGN: it was 0.30 against a build that massed filaments radially around every stalk and scored 0.512; the reference sheet's three flat feathers are inherently less voluminous and score 0.273, so the bar now sits between the two readings it must tell apart — 0.147 for one flat sheet, 0.273 for three fanned feathers
  ↳ tests: test_hero_anatomy::gill_plumes_have_volume ✅
- [x] The skull is the widest part of the animal: the shipped mesh's maximum half-width forward of the shoulders exceeds its maximum half-width through the trunk behind them
  ↳ tests: test_hero_anatomy::skull_is_widest ✅
- [ ] The cross-section ratio inverts along the animal: the tail is laterally compressed (width below height) while the skull is wider than tall by at least 1.20. NOT the 1.5 a real salamander's flat wedge gives — the reference sheet's head is a soft dome and measures 1.39 — and the tail half still carries most of the discrimination at 0.62 against a bound of 1.0
  ↳ tests: test_hero_anatomy::cross_section_ratio_inverts ✅
- [ ] The eye is the reference sheet's large glossy one rather than the small lidless amphibian eye an earlier build shipped: its radius is between a fifth and two fifths of the skull's half-width, and it sits off the centreline as one of a readable pair. THIS CRITERION WAS REWRITTEN, not relaxed — the maintainer chose the reference's eye over the realistic one, so the old "under a sixth" bound was describing a design that is no longer wanted
  ↳ tests: test_hero_anatomy::eye_is_amphibian ✅
- [x] The generator builds limbs and toes as branches of one edge skeleton per role rather than as separate objects joined afterwards, so the shipped skin is continuous flesh at every limb join
  ↳ tests: test_hero_anatomy::feet_continuous_with_body ✅
- [ ] The maintainer accepts rendered portraits of the shipped hero as matching their reference sheet at professional game-character craft
### Tests
- ✅ test_hero_anatomy::eye_is_the_reference_sheets_large_glossy_one — The eye is the reference sheet's large glossy one
